content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts peak too early and then plateau or slightly decline, while true prices often show sharper, delayed corrections or mean reversion.
- After a spike in price (e.g., 70s to 76s), model fails to capture subsequent pullback; overestimates remain high longer than actual.
- Model exhibits diminishing sensitivity to recent price drops — fails to adjust downward when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true price movements, missing volatility and sharp reversals.
- Model underreacts to low-price periods in recent history — fails to anticipate price dips when recent 7–10 days show downward trend.
- Forecasts often overshoot the true mean by 2–5% in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converge — suggesting a lag in recalibration.
- Model does not account for “recovery” or “reversal” patterns after sharp spikes — assumes continuation of trend.
- True prices often show a “reversion to mean” pattern after spikes, while model holds high forecasts longer than warranted.
- Model overweights recent high prices and underweights recent low prices — creates bias toward overestimating future prices.
